expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: Rests on i0, the most tightly linked peer document available (QFIN's 11-24 6-K exhibit: Q4 net income guided -67 to -77% YoY, 'clear erosion in risk performance', regulation into 2027) landing one day before FINV reports into the same channel and the same NFRA regime, with FINV down only 4.6% against QFIN's -11.2% on 11-25, so the read-through is demonstrably not absorbed; the next-guide direction is a cut (i1) and the one bull leg, the 27-30% overseas offset, is independently deteriorating in the September OJK TWP90 series (i5), which the US previews do not carry. The washed-out setup and sub-cash valuation with a live buyback (i3, i4, i7) are the offsets and are why p_up is 36 rather than lower.

opus55.note: Rests on Qfin's 2026-11-24 Q4 guide (net income down 67-77% YoY, 'clear erosion in risk performance'), a closely linked peer in the same channel that fell 11.2% while FINV fell only 4.6%; with FINV's last guide-driven prints at -13.9% and -15.4%, a further guide cut or a Qfin-style profit outlook outweighs the washed-out setup and the below-cash valuation.

sonnet55.note: Rests on QFIN's linked same-channel Q4 guide collapse (-11% on the day, FINV only -4.6%) and the likely FY cut; offset by a street already below the guide, a washed-out tape, rising short interest and a below-cash valuation with a live buyback.

fable51.note: Qfin's 11-24 print (same channel, same regulation, Q4 net income guided down 67-77%, credit erosion, QFIN -11.2%) landed after FINV last spoke and FINV absorbed only -4.6% of it; with the company's own July volume -50% warning, a likely FY revenue cut, no buy-side floor, and a name that fell 15.4% and 13.9% on its last two guide-driven prints, the cash-backed buyback and washed-out setup only partly offset a negative lean sized on the 17% straddle and the name's own print history.

opus5.note: The quarter is near-certainly weak (BCRA Sept group ROA 1.4->0.5, i0; BBAR -57.7% QoQ, i1; GGAL -16% and -12% vs consensus, i2) but the expectations items are heavier and almost cancel it: at a 52-week low, -7.65% across the peer-print week, 49% of target, with both brokers below consensus and still buy (i6, i9), a live buyback 80% unspent (i7), a board statement of undervaluation made inside the quarter (i8), and a peer whose 12% consensus miss cost only ~1% (i2); the residual negative is the stale 219.5bn headline (i4) and this name's habit of selling its own good prints (i10), damped further by a Thanksgiving half-session exit.

opus55.note: The BCRA September series (private domestic bank ROA ~1.4% to ~0.5%) and BBAR's >50% miss point to Macro missing even Citi's lower bar, but the stock sits at its 52-week low after a 7.65% peer-print week, GGAL's 12% miss cost only ~1%, the buyback is bidding and the 2027 guide comes after the window, so only a slight downward lean.

sonnet55.note: A miss against the 219.5bn consensus is well signalled by the BCRA series and the peer prints, but the stock sits at its 52-week low at 49% of targets with a live buyback, the real bar is Citi's ~189bn and the guide comes after the window, so the two sides roughly offset.

fable51.note: A peso miss against the stale Bloomberg 219.5bn is the base case (BCRA system ROA collapse, BBAR -58% QoQ, SUPV and GGAL misses), but the real bar is Citi's ~189bn, the stock sits at a 52-week low after falling 7.65% through the peer-print week, GGAL lost only ~1% on a 12% miss, a buyback bids through the window and the call with any guide is on 11-30 outside it, so the net is a small negative lean.

opus5.note: A near-zero: the stock is a 15.3% take-private spread to $6.03 (i0), so the quarter has little transmission and the release is very unlikely to carry a process update; the only honest lean is the Q2 credit trend (31-60d 2.61->1.73%, provision 52.3m->10.1m, profit +23.8% QoQ, i2) continuing into a Q3 profit print that nobody models on a one-stale-analyst name and that makes $6.03 against 0.2x book look low, set against continued volume shrinkage, a bidder-controlled cautious tone and an expiring buyback (i1, i4, i5), on a Black Friday half-session in a 100k-ADS name.

opus55.note: The $6.03 controller take-private bid anchors the stock as a 15% arb spread, so the quarter (lower volume, better credit) and a bidder-controlled cautious no-guide offset; nothing sourced says which way the spread moves in a half-day window.

sonnet55.note: The stock trades as a 15% arb spread to the $6.03 take-private bid with no consensus and no guide, so a routine release moves it little; slight positive lean from improving credit and possible process news.

fable51.note: The $6.03 controller bid anchors the price and the quarter has no sourced bar; a further volume shrink and a bidder-friendly cautious tone (both expected, no guide since Q2) offset a likely provision-driven profit uptick and the low-probability deal-update tail, so nothing in the pack moves the 15% arb spread with a sign and the name is a non-result on a thin half-day session.
